title: 初一四篇十五题：院落家、猫日记与颜色船
instruction: 阅读A、B、C、D四组完整材料，回答第1至第15题；每题从A、B、C、D四个选项中选出最合适的一项。每题2分，共30分。家庭、人物、猫日记、社团活动和幻想故事均为虚构。B组最后一条12 a.m.明确为次日开始的午夜。
source_notice: 参照苏州标签初一公开描述层完整阅读节：A导语加三位儿童居住简介，B猫第一人称六时点日记，C活动说明含规则/棋类思考比较/推荐，D完整幻想对话含一缺轮与四事件排序；四篇3+4+4+4共15四选，各2分共30分。源正文999词，原PDF及装饰图片有无未认证，完整指所选文字输入与全部候选，原键非gold；源C21B/C近义双支持、B15计划/完成及午夜日界歧义和原拼写/句点缺失保留。新稿为虚构，A家庭不是地区建筑普遍性调查，B午夜显式次日开始、下午已完成动作和后续计划分开。C以虚构社团目标活动保规则/先思考与推荐任务，不抄攀岩安全/健康论断，不代表正式运动规则或难度等值。D原创魔法设定非原著改写，缺轮与四事件顺序、角色行为和末尾未解决目标分别核对。每题唯一最佳的作者依据含全部四候选反证；三稿同源体裁/操作家族，非三独立来源，未作独立教研/学生/商用/生产验证。

sections.label: A
units:
Tari
Our house has a wide roof that reaches well beyond the walls. It gives shade to the windows during the hottest part of the day; that is why the roof was designed this way. We hang clean clothes under the edge when rain is expected. My favourite seat is beside the east window, where I read before breakfast.

June
My family lives in a converted railway carriage that stays in one place. The narrow rooms run in a line, and our kitchen is at one end. There are no train journeys from this home: the old wheels no longer move. We have a wooden deck outside, where I keep a small table for drawing on dry days.

Omar
Our house faces a **courtyard**, an open space enclosed by the rooms around it. My cousins live in the rooms opposite ours. We can talk across the space, but we do not play noisy games there after dark. A tree in the middle gives us shade. In summer we sometimes sit beneath it and share stories before going indoors.
sections.intro: These three children have been asked to explain a feature of their home. Read their descriptions of the buildings and daily life.

sections.label: B
units:
My human is preparing for a small music evening at home. I, Moss the cat, intend to be part of the performance. Here is what happened.

5 a.m. — A low note came from the next room. A wonderful new sound! I hurried towards it with my tail high. My human was testing a small keyboard before breakfast. I was certain that she had invented this exciting sound especially for me.

7 a.m. — I stepped onto one key and made a note of my own. My human picked me up and put me on the rug. She said she needed to practise. I waited for her to invite me back, but she carried on playing without my help.

8 a.m. — My human put a cover over the keyboard and went shopping. She left a soft toy fish on the rug. I watched the door, hoping that she would return with an instrument of the right size for me. The toy did not make any sound at all.

3 p.m. — I have already chased the toy fish across the rug and hidden it under a cushion. That filled my afternoon nicely. Later I will curl up in the empty music case, but I have not climbed into it yet. I am too busy listening for the front door.

9 p.m. — The guests arrived and the music began. My human kept the keyboard on a tall stand. I called out once to join in. Everyone laughed, but nobody offered me a turn at the keys. A pat on the head is pleasant, yet it is not the same as performing.

12 a.m. (start of the next day) — It is now midnight at the beginning of the next day. The guests have left. My human says it was a successful evening. I had imagined playing beside her, but I remained an audience member on the rug. Next time I shall need a better plan.

sections.label: C
units:
At our fictional club, Colour Court is a new throwing game. Players toss cloth bags towards three coloured squares on the floor. A bag earns points only if it lands completely inside one square. The smallest square offers the highest score. This is an invented activity for our story, not an account of a standard competitive sport.

Our club has a clear rule: take your throw from behind the white line. A player may practise the movement before the round, but cannot step over the line to get closer to a square. After each throw, the leader notes where the bag has stopped and removes it before the next turn. Everyone in that round uses the same line and the same set of targets.

It may look like a test of strength, but a powerful throw can fly over every square. A player chooses a target, judges the distance and decides on a movement. Chess also asks you to think about a move before making it. The games are different, but planning matters in both. After seeing the result, a player can reconsider the next attempt.

I like having to choose between an easy target and a harder one. People who enjoy making a plan and learning from its result may find Colour Court interesting. Start with a simple round and see what you think. The writer does not claim that this game is best for everyone or that it produces a particular health effect.

sections.label: D
units:
Lina wanted a little boat to carry her to the island garden. The boatman’s notice said, “Wear your own colour to step aboard.” But her coat had changed from yellow to silver to blue since breakfast, without her touching it. She needed to find out which colour was really hers. She had brought her lunch already, so this was not a search for something to eat.

Lina searched the grass at the edge of the landing place. Beneath a bent reed she found a round mirror no bigger than a plate. A green moth rested on its handle, slowly folding a paper hat. Lina watched until the moth looked at her. “What colour are you wearing?” it asked.

“▲,” she said. “A moment ago it was blue. Before that it was silver. I cannot see my back, and it may have changed again.”

“You should know your own coat,” said the moth crossly.

Lina described all three colours and asked if she could use the mirror. “Then I might be able to answer you properly,” she said.

“First answer my question,” said the moth, holding the mirror face down. It offered no explanation for the changes and did not let Lina look. She felt that they were only going round the same problem.

Lina turned towards the path. “Wait,” called the moth. “There is a secret about that boat.” She came back, hoping to hear it. The moth unfolded its hat and pointed towards the water, but had not yet spoken again. Lina’s coat flashed silver. She was still on the landing place, and she had neither used the mirror nor boarded the boat.

questions.stem: A组 · Why does Tari’s home have a roof wider than the walls?
options: To shade the windows in the hottest hours.
To give the cousins opposite a new room.
To keep every window dark all day.
To allow a train to pass through the rooms.
questions.rationale: A：设计原因明确遮热时窗；B：堂亲是Omar家且未扩房；C：仅最热时遮阳非整天黑暗；D：无列车穿屋

options: An open space surrounded by rooms.
A wide roof above the windows.
A road used for evening traffic.
A long kitchen inside an old train.
questions.rationale: A：后文定义围绕房间的开敞空间；B：Tari屋顶非词义；C：院内非道路交通；D：列车厨房属June且非词义

questions.stem: A组 · Which statement is true according to the descriptions?
options: June’s railway-carriage home stays in one place.
Tari reads by the west window after dinner.
June draws on her outdoor table in all weather.
Omar plays noisy courtyard games after dark.
questions.rationale: A：明确轮不动无从家出发列车旅行；B：东窗早餐前；C：只dry days；D：明确天黑后不玩吵闹游戏

questions.stem: B组 · What is Moss’s first reaction to the low note?
options: He is bored with the new sound.
He is worried about the guests leaving.
He is angry that the fish is silent.
He is excited to investigate it.
questions.rationale: A：兴奋非无聊；B：首条尚未宾客，非离开；C：鱼在8点，非最初反应；D：wonderful且尾高急赴声源

questions.stem: B组 · By 3 p.m., what has Moss already done?
options: Performed at the keyboard for the guests.
Chased the fish and hidden it under a cushion.
Climbed into the empty music case.
Brought an instrument home from the shop.
questions.rationale: A：宾客晚到且未让上键；B：already完整追藏玩具动作；C：明确not climbed yet；D：人购物，未给猫乐器

questions.stem: B组 · What does Moss think about the evening with his human?
options: He believes no music was played at all.
He did not get the performing role he wanted.
He played beside her exactly as he planned.
He did not want to take part in the music.
questions.rationale: A：音乐确实开始且宾客听；B：想并肩弹，结果观众；C：明确没有；D：多条表明想加入

questions.stem: B组 · Which title is best for the whole diary?
options: A Cat Hopes to Join the Music
The Guests’ Trip to a Music Shop
A Fish That Learns to Sing
questions.rationale: A：非维修步骤；B：整日猫盼加入乐演；C：宾客未去乐器店；D：玩具不会响无学唱

questions.stem: C组 · Where is this article most likely to appear?
options: In a catalogue of kitchen furniture.
In a collection of garden poems.
In a book of train timetables.
questions.rationale: A：无家具商品目录；B：虚构社团投掷游戏介绍；C：非诗且非园艺；D：无列车时刻

questions.stem: C组 · What is a rule in this club’s Colour Court?
options: Use a different starting line from everyone else.
Leave each bag on the target for the next player.
Step over the line before every throw.
Throw from behind the white line.
questions.rationale: A：同轮同线；B：每投后移走；C：明确不可越线靠近；D：明确白线后投掷

questions.stem: C组 · What feature does Colour Court share with chess in the article?
options: Thinking about an action before taking it.
Using three cloth bags as playing pieces.
Trying to throw over every target.
Counting points before any move is made.
questions.rationale: A：两者均计划行动；B：棋不以布袋为器材；C：投过全部靶反而不好，棋非投掷；D：投后看停点，非先计分

questions.stem: C组 · Who does the writer suggest might enjoy Colour Court?
options: Players who dislike choosing a target.
Only people who can always hit the smallest square.
People who like planning and learning from results.
Everyone who wants a promised health effect.
questions.rationale: A：作者喜欢选择目标，非推荐反意；B：未限定高手，建议简单一轮；C：结尾推荐对象明确；D：明说不承诺健康效果

questions.stem:
D组 · Which is the correct order of Lina’s actions?

a. She asked to use the mirror after describing her coat.

b. She found a round mirror.

c. She searched the grass.

d. She gave her first answer to the moth.
questions.rationale: A：请求在初答之后；B：初答发生在发现镜之后；C：搜草、发现镜、初答、描述并请求；D：不是发现后再找

options: It has been yellow since breakfast without changing
The mirror has already shown me the answer
I cannot be certain just now
I have never worn a coat today
questions.rationale: A：明确先黄再银再蓝；B：末文未用镜且镜朝下；C：颜色随时变且看不到背部，当前不确定；D：首段一直穿变色外套

questions.stem: D组 · How does the moth behave in this conversation?
options: Frightened into silence from the start.
Helpful because it has already stopped the changes.
Kind and ready to lend the mirror at once.
questions.rationale: A：反复说话并非始终不语；B：外套末尾仍变银；C：crossly说话且镜朝下不让看；D：拒绝借镜先让答

questions.stem: D组 · What is clear at the end of the story?
options: The moth has finished telling the boat’s secret.
Lina needs the mirror to find her missing lunch.
Lina has used the mirror and chosen one fixed colour.
Lina has not boarded the boat yet.
questions.rationale: A：手指水面但未再次说话；B：已有午餐，镜为看色；C：未用镜仍变色；D：末句明确仍登船处未上船
